item.title: 450 cartons of bottled water collected for drought-affected communities
item.description: A total of 450 cartons of bottled water have been collected through the Fiji Drought One Drop Bottle Water Appeal. The appeal has been organised by Sawani resident Sandeep Prakash, who is calling on members of the public to donate at least one bottle or carton of water to help families affected by the drought.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 450 cartons of bottled water have been collected through the Fiji Drought One Drop Bottle Water Appeal.

The appeal has been organised by Sawani resident Sandeep Prakash, who is calling on members of the public to donate at least one bottle or carton of water to help families affected by the drought.

He says, with the water collected so far, he will begin delivering supplies to affected communities in the Western Division on Monday.

Prakash says distribution will begin in the Tavua area, working with Advisory Councillor Hirdesh Nand to reach families who do not have Water Authority of Fiji meters.

He says the team then plans to continue to Ba, visiting communities in Moto Hill, Vatsui, Nukuloa, Tabataba and Waiwai.

Prakash has thanked people in Fiji and overseas who have contributed to the appeal, saying their generosity will help provide drinking water to families in need.

Members of the public who wish to donate bottled water can drop it off at his residence in Sawani, Nausori, beside the Royal Event Centre, at any time.

Those wishing to assist can also contact Prakash on 8610909.

item.title: Boy, 3, dies after being struck by vehicle at NSW holiday park
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/11/2026 A three-year-old boy has passed away after being hit by a small utility vehicle at a holiday park on the New South Wales Central Coast in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/11/2026

A three-year-old boy has passed away after being hit by a small utility vehicle at a holiday park on the New South Wales Central Coast in Australia.

Emergency services were called to the Blue Lagoon Beach Resort on Bateau Bay Road yesterday evening , following reports that a child had been hit by a vehicle.

Paramedics attempted to treat the toddler at the scene, but he could not be revived.

The driver of the Mitsubishi Triton, a 47-year-old man, was arrested and taken to hospital for mandatory testing.

A crime scene was established and examined by specialist officers.

Police say the driver was not related to the boy.

Preliminary evidence suggests the ute was travelling at a low speed, but investigations are ongoing.
